newsitem.title: USA: Andrew Corp slides after downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Andrew Corp slides after downgrade.

text.p: Shares of Andrew Corp fell about 20 percent Tuesday after the telecommunications equipment company's rating was cut by a Minneapolis-based analyst.
An analyst at Wessels, Arnold & Henderson Llc cut Andrew Corp to hold from buy-growth, due to concerns about the company's revenue stream, sources familiar with the report said.
The analyst also cut his revenue estimate for the fiscal year ending in September to $922.2 million from $947.2 million, compared to $793.6 million a year ago, sources said.
Merrill Lynch also cut Andrew Corp to near-term neutral from accumulate, but kept the long-term rating accumulate.

Andrew Corp's broadcasting business could be weaker than expected in the near term because of the impending switch from traditional to high-definition television, the Wessel, Arnold & Henderson analyst said in a research note, according to sources.

Also, a sales shift in wireless accessories to products with stronger sales in the December quarter could mean progression in the business could be rough for the rest of fiscal 1997, the analyst said, according to sources.

But slightly better than expected gross margins could offset the near-term revenue problems, so the analyst left his fiscal 1997 earnings estimate at $1.24 a share, compared to $0.98 a share a year ago, sources said.
Wessels, Arnold & Henderson said it does not comment to reporters.
Andrew Corp shares were down 5-3/8 at 24 Tuesday.
